title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
contract: Return the length of the longest run of consecutive integer values, regardless of input order. Duplicates do not extend a run.
brute: int best=0;for(int start:a){long value=start;int length=0;while(value<=Integer.MAX_VALUE){boolean found=false;for(int x:a)if(x==value){found=true;break;}if(!found)break;length++;value++;}best=Math.max(best,length);emit("Scan for each successor","start",start,"length",length,"best",best);}return best;
optimal: Set<Long> values=new HashSet<>();for(int x:a)values.add((long)x);int best=0;for(long start:values)if(!values.contains(start-1)){long value=start;while(values.contains(value))value++;best=Math.max(best,(int)(value-start));emit("Extend only from a run's smallest value","start",start,"length",value-start,"best",best);}return best;
reasoning: For every starting value, repeatedly scan the input for its successor.
A value begins a maximal run only when its predecessor is absent.
Start expansion only at those minima, so each distinct value participates in one run. Use long keys to keep predecessor/successor arithmetic safe at int boundaries.
